dependencies.reason: builds its CLI commands on the client, output and exit-code helpers of the CLI foundation
validates and matches the targets of a rule with the branch-glob functions of internal/workspace/branchglob.go
evaluation reads a change's state, target branch, current version, touched files and mergeable from the change records of package 22 and stores the result as the change's landing
runs its landable announcement, the one writer of parley.change.ready, in every transaction that stores a landing
registers its evaluation as the policy gate that internal/land declares
emits its hub events through the event log component

tasks.title: Validate a policy document and produce its normal form
steps: Add the accepted-document table, the shared table of invalid documents, the unknown-username cases, the limit cases and the first-violation cases to internal/policy/document_test.go and confirm they fail

Define the document: default and an ordered list of rules (name, paths, exclude, targets, require), and the requirement (approvals, approvers, checks, fresh_checks, block), decoded from JSON text so that a member of the wrong JSON type is told apart from an absent one

Define the invalid-policy error carrying rule (name, 'default' or null), index (zero-based position or null) and field (member name, prefixed 'require.' inside a rule, with '[i]' for one entry), and the narrow user lookup the validator asks whether a username exists, in internal/policy/ports.go

Validate in the fixed order and stop at the first violation: text longer than 65 536 bytes (field 'document'); text that is not a JSON object ('document'); top-level member types; more than 200 rules ('rules'); default; then each rule in order by name, paths, exclude, targets, require

Check a rule name against ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$, refuse 'default' and a name an earlier rule has; check each path glob for 1 to 255 characters and no leading '/'; check each targets entry with ValidateBranchGlob of package 11 in internal/workspace/branchglob.go (a branch name of 1 to 255 characters in which * and ** may appear, by the branch-name rule quoted in the package PRD), writing no second validator; refuse an empty paths list and a targets list that is present and empty

Check a requirement: approvals an integer from 0 to 10; approvers, when present, non-empty with entries 'owner', 'member' or 'user:<username>' whose username the lookup knows; each check name against ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,62}$; fresh_checks and block booleans. Return a lookup failure as itself, never as an invalid-policy error

Produce the normal form of an accepted document: default always present, all five requirement members filled with their defaults, exclude filled with an empty list, targets kept only where given, undefined members dropped, and make validating a normal form return it unchanged

tasks.title: Match globs and select the governing rule for a file
steps: Add the path-glob table to internal/policy/glob_test.go and the target table and the rule-selection table to internal/policy/evaluate_test.go and confirm they fail

Match a path glob against a whole repository-relative path: * is any run without '/', possibly empty; ** is any run, possibly empty; a longer run of asterisks reads as ** followed by the rest; ? is exactly one character other than '/'; every other character, '[' and '\' included, is itself; matching is case-sensitive

Match a targets entry against the change's target branch with MatchAnyBranchGlob of package 11 (internal/workspace/branchglob.go), in which '?' is an ordinary character; write no branch matcher here, and use the path matcher of this task for policy paths and exclude only, never for the paths of a token, which package 06's matcher decides
Keep matching free of exponential backtracking: a glob of 255 characters made of alternating * and letters against a 4 096-character path returns within the unit test's default time

Select for one file and one target branch the first rule in document order whose targets is absent or matches the branch, whose paths matches the file and whose exclude does not; return 'default' when none qualifies

tasks.title: Turn the selections of a change into requirements and a landing status
steps: Add the requirement-shape, satisfaction, status, structural-reason, empty-change, no-evidence and failure tables to internal/policy/evaluate_test.go with stubbed change facts and evidence, and confirm they fail

Define in internal/policy/ports.go the change facts the evaluator works on (number, current version, state, target branch, mergeable, the structural reason the record carries, the touched files) and the evidence source: one question per requirement, given the workspace, the change, its current version, the requirement's approvers, its check names and its fresh_checks, answering the counted approvals, whether a counted rejection is outstanding, and a status per check name that has a result

Provide the evidence source that answers nothing (0 counted, no rejection, no check result) as the one installed at first, and a registration function that replaces the installed source, which package 28 calls with its own

Group the change's files by selected rule; build one requirement per distinct selection in document order with default last; list its files in ascending byte order cut to the first 50; list each check name of the rule once in the rule's order, with status pending where the evidence has no result
Mark a requirement satisfied exactly when block is false, counted is at least required, no counted rejection is outstanding and every named check is passed

Derive the result {status, reason, requirements}: a draft change is blocked with reason draft; otherwise a structural reason on the record gives blocked with that reason; otherwise blocked with reason null when a requirement blocks, pending when one is unsatisfied, ready when all are satisfied or there is none. Requirements are listed in every case
Offer a second mode used by the evaluate route: no evidence is asked, counted is 0, every check is pending and structural reasons are not applied
Return a failure of the file read or of the evidence source as the evaluation's failure, with no partial result

tasks.title: Keep policy revisions and serve GET policy
steps: Add the read cases (never set, current, by revision, not kept or malformed revision, fork, member and fork-bound and archived readers, refusals) to internal/policy/handlers_test.go against a hub started in-process, and confirm they fail

Register a schema step with internal/store for a table of policy revisions keyed by workspace slug and revision, holding the normal-form document, updated_at and the writer's actor_type, actor_id and username

Read the current revision of a workspace and one revision by number in internal/policy/store.go; a workspace with no row, and every task fork, has the revision-0 document with updated_at and updated_by null; revision 0 is readable only while no row exists

Register GET /workspaces/:slug/policy with internal/server with scope changes:read and need read, so that the scope, access and binding answers come from the shared pipeline; define in internal/policy/ports.go the narrow workspace lookup the handlers need (kind, status, default branch)

Answer 200 with {revision, default, rules, updated_at, updated_by} and the header ETag with the revision in double quotes; answer 404 not_found for a revision that is not kept and 400 invalid_request for a revision value that is not a non-negative integer
Wire the policy component into parleyd's start so the route is served by the real hub

tasks.title: Replace the policy with PUT under an optional revision condition
steps: Add the replace cases (store and answer, the event, If-Match mismatch, invalid input, fork and archived, caller refusals, concurrent writers) to internal/policy/handlers_test.go and the 52-replacement retention case to internal/policy/store_test.go, and confirm they fail

Register PUT /workspaces/:slug/policy with scope workspaces:write and need owner; the route is not among the routes a fork-bound token reaches on its parent, so the binding guard answers 403 token_bound there

After access, decide in this order: a task fork is 400 not_supported_on_fork; a body that is not a JSON object or an If-Match that is not a non-negative integer, bare or in double quotes, is 400 invalid_request; an invalid document is 400 invalid_policy with details {rule, index, field} from the validator, the size being the byte length of the body; an archived workspace is 409 workspace_archived; an If-Match that differs from the stored revision is 412 revision_mismatch
Use the real user lookup over the identity data for user:<username> approvers

In one store transaction: read the stored revision, compare it with If-Match, write the normal form as revision stored + 1 with the caller as updated_by and the current time, delete revisions numbered new - 50 or lower, and hand parley.policy.update (resource_type policy, resource_id the slug, action update, actor the caller, metadata revision and rules count) to the event component; a failure of any part rolls all of it back and answers 500 internal
Make the revision read and the write one serialised step, so that two concurrent replacements get consecutive revisions and two with the same If-Match yield one 200 and one 412

Answer 200 with the body and ETag that GET returns for the new revision; leave a hook, run inside the same transaction before commit, where the re-evaluation of the workspace's changes is attached later

tasks.title: Read a change's files and keep its stored landing current
steps: Add the rename, stacked-base and 2 100-file cases to internal/policy/changeadapter_test.go and the store-and-return, ready-event table, closed, not-found, failure and fork-target cases to internal/policy/reevaluate_test.go, and confirm they fail

Implement the change facts over the change records of internal/change and internal/gitrepo: state, target workspace and branch, current version, mergeable, the structural reason on the record, and the files that differ between the current version's base_sha and head_sha with both paths of every rename and no cap

Offer the operation 're-evaluate change N of workspace W': inside one store transaction read the current policy revision of the change's target workspace (the revision-0 document for a task fork), evaluate with the installed evidence source, write the result as the change's landing and return the result with the revision

After the landing is written, run the landable announcement that package 23 exports from internal/change/landable.go in the same transaction: it alone writes parley.change.ready (actor system, metadata number, ref, version, head_sha) when the change is open, ready and clean for a head not yet announced, and forgets the announcement when the change is no longer landable; write no event of that type in internal/policy

Return the change-closed error for a landed or abandoned change and the change-not-found error for an unknown number or slug, writing nothing in either case; roll back the landing when the event cannot be recorded

Wire the operation into parleyd: register it as the landing evaluator of the change component of package 22 (opening, new version, retarget, draft/open moves) and as the policy gate that package 25 declares in internal/land (answering status, reason, requirements and revision), each in place of the everything-is-ready default, and expose it for package 28 to call after an approval, a withdrawal and a check report

tasks.title: Re-evaluate every draft and open change when the policy is replaced
steps: Add the after-update cases (all changes follow, ready events, evidence kept, closed changes untouched, failure rolls back, concurrent single re-evaluation) to internal/policy/reevaluate_test.go and confirm they fail
List the draft and open changes whose target workspace is the workspace, in ascending number order, through the change facts

Attach to the PUT's transaction hook: evaluate each listed change against the new document, write its landing and run the landable announcement of package 23 for it, so that each open, clean change whose status moved to ready gets one parley.change.ready, all before the transaction commits and before the 200 is sent
Read approvals and checks only through the evidence source; delete or change none
Fail the whole PUT with 500 internal when any change's evaluation or write fails, leaving the revision, the document, every landing and the event log as before

Make a single-change re-evaluation read the policy revision inside its own write transaction, so that one racing with a policy update either runs before it and is overwritten by the update's pass or runs after it against the new revision

tasks.title: Answer what paths or a change would need without writing anything
steps: Add the evaluate cases (paths, change, candidate policy, nothing written, invalid requests, invalid candidate, unknown or foreign change, caller refusals) to internal/policy/handlers_test.go and confirm they fail
Register POST /workspaces/:slug/policy/evaluate with scope changes:read and need read; it creates no resource

Validate the body: exactly one of paths and change; paths of 1 to 2 000 non-empty strings without a leading '/', repeated entries counted once; change an integer; target_branch refused together with change, when empty and past 255 characters; paths without target_branch on a workspace with no default branch is refused; each is 400 invalid_request
Validate a candidate policy with the validator, its size being the byte length of the member's JSON text, and answer 400 invalid_policy with the validator's details when it is refused

With change, read the change's files and target branch in whatever state it is; answer 404 change_not_found for an unknown number and, with identical body, for a caller that is a token bound to a task fork when the change's source workspace is not that fork

Evaluate in the no-evidence, no-structural-reason mode against the candidate, else the stored document, else the revision-0 document for a task fork, for target_branch or the default branch, and answer 200 {policy_revision: the stored revision, status, requirements}
Open no write transaction on this route: no revision, no event and no landing changes

tasks.title: Add parley policy get, set and evaluate
steps: Add the get, set, TOML and standard input, evaluate and usage-error cases to internal/cli/policy_test.go against a fake hub and confirm they fail
Declare the command group policy with get, set and evaluate through the command helper of internal/cli, each with its method and path and one positional argument, the slug
policy get: optional --revision, a non-negative integer, sent as the query revision; print the response body

Read a policy file for --file and --policy-file: '-' is standard input; a name ending in .toml is decoded as TOML; anything else is decoded as JSON and, when that fails, as TOML; the TOML table default and array of tables rules become the JSON document; a file that cannot be read or decodes as neither is a usage error

policy set: required --file; optional --if-revision, a non-negative integer, sent as the header If-Match with the number in double quotes; send the document with PUT as application/json and print the response body

policy evaluate: exactly one of --paths (comma-separated, repeatable, order kept) and --change (a non-negative integer); optional --target as target_branch and --policy-file as policy; send POST and print the response body
Report every usage error before any request with exit status 2 and the usage_error envelope on stderr, through the shared error path of internal/cli

Add the two end-to-end scenarios (set a policy and read the changes; evaluate and a refused set with a fork-bound token) to test/e2e/policy_test.go, driving the real command tree against a hub started in-process
